title: Bus, Tram & Cycle Lanes
whatItIs: Lanes kept for buses, trams or cycles, shown by signs and road markings. Some apply only at certain times.
keyFacts: Bus lanes are marked by a thick white line and signs showing which vehicles may use them and when.
Don't drive in a bus lane during its times of operation unless the sign allows your vehicle.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT drive or park in a cycle lane marked by a solid white line during its times of operation.

keyFacts: Don't drive or park in a cycle lane marked by a broken white line unless it's unavoidable.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT enter a road, lane or route reserved for trams.

visual.caption: Lanes reserved for some road users

items.label: Bus lane
items.meaning: Thick white line. Check the sign for times and who may use it.

items.label: Mandatory cycle lane
items.meaning: Solid line: you MUST NOT drive or park in it during its times.

items.label: Advisory cycle lane
items.meaning: Broken line: don't drive or park in it unless unavoidable.

a.label: Solid cycle lane line
points: MUST NOT drive or park in it

onTheTest.question: A bus lane sign shows no times. When is the bus lane in operation?
onTheTest.why: If no times are shown, the bus lane is in operation all day, every day.

traps: No times on a bus lane sign means it operates 24 hours a day.
Some bus lanes also allow taxis or cycles: the sign shows which.
Don't stop on tram tracks: a tram can't steer around you.

review.notes: Confirm the 24-hour rule for bus lanes without times in Know Your Traffic Signs.
